raw_text:
Thanks for the context. Here’s a 12-week strength-focused program for a 30-year-old advanced lifter who is 20 weeks pregnant, with OB clearance for moderate strength work. It respects pregnancy contraindications (no supine position after week 16, no max attempts, no contact sports) and prioritizes safety, posture, and gradual progression while preserving strength and conditioning.

Assumptions and guidelines
- Frequency: 4 days per week (e.g., Mon Tue off Wed Thu). You can adjust to 3 days if needed, but 4 days allows you to maintain volume without excessive fatigue.
- Intensity: Moderate effort most days; avoid to full failure. Reps in Reserve (RIR) guidance can help: aim for 1–2 RIR on most sets, 0–1 RIR on key movements only if comfortable.
- Positions: No supine after ~16 weeks. Use seated, standing, incline/semi-recline, or supported positions (back-supported bench with slight incline, racked goblet, seated row). For core, use breathing-based or anti-rotation work; avoid lying flat on back after mid-pregnancy.
- Core: Emphasize safe, progressive core and pelvic floor work; avoid traditional crunches or V-ups. Include diaphragmatic breathing, dead bugs, Pallof presses, transverse abdominis activation, and bird-dogs with progressive loading.
- Cardiovascular: Light to moderate, as tolerated, 2–3 days/week, 20–30 minutes, mostly at conversational pace. If desired, incorporate light intervals later for conditioning.
- Nutrition: Emphasize adequate protein (roughly 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day if tolerated), calories to support pregnancy and training, hydration, and iron/folate as advised by OB. Include vitamin recommendations per OB.
- Recovery: Prioritize sleep, hydration, stretching, and light mobility. Consider 5–10 minutes of mobility pre/post each session; avoid overtraining symptoms (dizziness, unusual shortness of breath, headaches).

Program structure
- Phase 1: Foundation and stabilization (Weeks 1–4)
- Phase 2: Volume and maintenance with safe progression (Weeks 5–8)
- Phase 3: Strength maintenance and performance-oriented work with reduced loads and safer alternatives (Weeks 9–12)

Week-by-week plan

Weeks 1–4: Foundation and stabilization
Goal: Rebuild movement quality, establish safe patterns, and maintain strength with moderate loads.

Session structure (4 days/week)
- Warm-up: 5–7 minutes light cardio + dynamic mobility (hips, thoracic spine, shoulders) + gentle activation drills (glute bridges, bird-dogs, scapular activation)
- Main lifts: two lower-load, non-supine patterns; two upper-body patterns, all with controlled tempo (2–0–2 or 3–0–2)
- Accessory work: 2–3 exercises focusing on posterior chain, rotator cuff, core, and anti-rotation
- Cool-down: Mobility and breathing work; 3–5 minutes

Week 1
- Day A
  - Box/Supported Squat (high-bar or goblet): 3 sets x 8 reps @ RPE 6 (comfortable)
  - Romanian Deadlift (DB or barbell, moderate load, but avoid excessive lumbar flexion): 3x8 @ RPE 6
  - Seated Dumbbell Overhead Press: 3x10 @ RPE 6
  - Inverted Row or Supported Row (TRX or barbell with incline): 3x10
  - Core: Pallof press (standing) 3x8 per side
- Day B
  - Split Squat with support (bench behind for balance): 3x8 per leg @ RPE 6
  - Hip Thrust or Glute Bridge (feet supported): 3x10 @ RPE 6
  - Dumbbell Bench Press or Incline Press (seated if necessary): 3x10
  - Lat Pulldown or Assisted Pull-Up: 3x8
  - Core: Dead Bug progressions 3x6 per side

Week 2
- Same structure, increase load slightly on 2–3 sets if RPE was 6 in Week 1 (target RPE 6–7)
- Day A: Squat 3x8 @ RPE 6–7; RDL 3x8 @ RPE 6–7; Seated DB Shoulder Press 3x10 @ RPE 6–7; Seated Row 3x10; Pallof press 3x8
- Day B: Split Squat 3x8 per leg; Hip Thrust 3x10; Incline DB Press 3x10; Lat Pulldown 3x8; Core as Week 1

Week 3
- Similar pattern; add one more set to 4x8 on primary lifts if tolerating
- Day A: Box/Squat 4x8; RDL 4x8; Seated DB Press 3x10; Seated Row 3x10; Pallof press 3x8
- Day B: Split Squat 4x6–8 per leg; Hip Thrust 3x12; Incline DB Press 3x10; Lat Pulldown 3x8; Core: Dead Bug 3x8

Week 4
- Deload/technique focus
- Day A: Squat 3x6 @ RPE 6–7; RDL 3x6; Seated Shoulder Press 3x8; Seated Row 3x8; Pallof press 3x6
- Day B: Split Squat 3x6 per leg; Glute Bridge 3x8; Incline DB Press 3x8; Lat Pulldown 3x8; Core: Bird-Dog 3x10 per side

Weeks 5–8: Volume and safe progression
Goal: Maintain or increase strength with controlled volume, introduce light power and rotate patterns.

Week 5
- Day A
  - Front/Back Squat alternative: goblet squat 4x6-8 or tempo squat 3x6
  - Hip Hunch/Glute Bridge: 3x8
  - Dumbbell Bench Press or Incline Press: 3x8
  - Seated Dumbbell Row: 3x8
  - Core: Pallof press 3x8 per side
- Day B
  - Bulgarian Split Squat or Elevated Split Squat: 3x6–8 per leg
  - Hip Thrust 3x8–10
  - Seated Arnold Press or Seated Military Press: 3x8
  - Lat Pulldown or Assisted Pull-Up: 3x8
  - Core: Anti-rotation carry (light) 3x20–30 seconds per side

Week 6
- Increase loads slightly if Week 5 was comfortable
- Day A
  - Goblet Front Squat or Front Squat (light): 4x6
  - RDL or Sumo RDL: 3x8
  - Seated DB Push Press: 3x8
  - Seated Row or Chest-Supported Row: 3x8
  - Core: Pallof press 3x8
- Day B
  - Bulgarian Split Squat 3x8 per leg
  - Hip Thrust 3x10
  - Incline DB Press 3x8
  - Lat Pulldown 3x8
  - Core: Dead Bug 3x8 per side

Week 7
- Similar to Week 5, but push closer to RPE 7 on main lifts
- Day A: Squat pattern 4x6; RDL 3x8; Seated Shoulder Press 3x8; Seated Row 3x8; Pallof press 3x8
- Day B: Split Squat 4x6 per leg; Hip Thrust 3x8; Incline DB Press 3x8; Lat Pulldown 3x8; Core: Bird-Dog 3x10 per side

Week 8
- Deload/technique emphasis
- Day A: Squat 3x5 at light-to-moderate load; RDL 3x6; Seated DB Press 3x8; Seated Row 3x8; Core: Pallof press 3x6
- Day B: Split Squat 3x6 per leg; Hip Thrust 3x8; Incline DB Press 3x8; Lat Pulldown 3x8; Core: Anti-rotation carry 3x20–30s

Weeks 9–12: Strength maintenance with safe adaptations
Goal: Maintain strength while reducing spinal load and avoiding supine positioning. Introduce occasional slight performance-oriented work with careful monitoring.

Week 9
- Day A
  - Goblet Squat or Chair-Assisted Front Squat: 4x5–6
  - Hip Thrust: 3x8
  - Seated Dumbbell Press: 3x8
  - Seated Row or Chest-Supported Row: 3x8
  - Core: Pallof press 3x8 per side
- Day B
  - Bulgarian Split Squat: 3x6 per leg
  - Hip Thrust or Glute Bridge: 3x8
  - Incline Dumbbell Press: 3x8
  - Lat Pulldown: 3x8
  - Core: Dead Bug 3x8 per side

Week 10
- Day A
  - Front/Back Squat alternative: goblet squat 4x5
  - Romanian Deadlift: 3x6
  - Seated Shoulder Press: 3x8
  - Seated Row: 3x8
  - Core: Pallof press 3x6
- Day B
  - Reverse Lunges or Split Squat: 3x6 per leg
  - Hip Thrust: 3x8
  - Incline DB Press: 3x8
  - Lat Pulldown: 3x8
  - Core: Anti-rotation carry 3x20–30s

Week 11
- Slightly higher load if tolerated; maintain volume
- Day A
  - Goblet Front Squat 4x5
  - RDL 3x6
  - Seated DB Push Press 3x8
  - Chest-Supported Row 3x8
  - Core: Pallof press 3x6
- Day B
  - Bulgarian Split Squat 3x6 per leg
  - Hip Thrust 3x8
  - Incline DB Bench Press 3x8
  - Lat Pulldown 3x8
  - Core: Dead Bug 3x8

Week 12
- Deload and technique refinement
- Day A
  - Goblet Squat 3x6
  - Hip Hinge movement: Hip Thrust 3x6
  - Seated Shoulder Press 3x6
  - Seated Row 3x6
  - Core: Pallof press 3x6
- Day B
  - Split Squat 3x6 per leg
  - Hip Bridge 3x6
  - Incline DB Press 3x6
  - Lat Pulldown 3x6
  - Core: Anti-rotation carry 3x20–30s

Exercise alternatives and safety notes
- Supine positions: Avoid lying on back after 16 weeks. Use incline bench, seated, kneeling, or standing patterns.
- Max attempts: Do not perform true 1RM tests. Use RPE or Reps In Reserve to gauge effort.
- Core sequence: Work on breathing, pelvic floor engagement, and safe anti-rotation exercises. Avoid crunches, V-ups, or any movement causing rib flare or doming.
- Posture and breathing: Maintain neutral spine; exhale on exertion and inhale on release where appropriate.
- Movement tempo: 2–0–2 or 3–0–2 tempo on most sets to control force and reduce intra-abdominal pressure spikes.
- Progression: Small weight increments (2.5–5 lb) on upper body and 5–10 lb on lower body if tolerated week-over-week, ensuring form remains clean.

Conditioning and recovery
- Gentle cardio: 2–3 days/week, 20–30 minutes, at a comfortable pace. If energy allows, incorporate light intervals (e.g., 1 minute moderate, 1 minute easy) sparingly.
- Mobility: 5–10 minutes daily focusing on hips, thoracic spine, and shoulders.
- Pelvic floor: Include Kegels or pelvic floor activation daily as advised by OB or physical therapist.
- Sleep and stress: Prioritize sleep hygiene; manage fatigue with adjustments to volume and intensity as needed.
- Hydration and nutrition: Keep hydration up; ensure prenatal nutrition aligns with OB guidance. Protein intake 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day if tolerated; caloric intake adequate to support growth and training.

Notes for the trainer
- Monitor for signs of overexertion: dizziness, lightheadedness, syncope, cramping, vaginal bleeding, or severe shortness of breath. If any occur, reduce load or skip the set.
- Adjust for pregnancy progression: By Week 28–32, consider further reducing supine time, adjust overhead pressing height, and reduce axial loading as needed.
- Communication: Check in weekly on energy, nausea, pain, or discomfort. Modify parameters accordingly.
- Consider individualized substitutions: If back pain arises, switch to more supported Rowing movements or chest-supported variations. If wrist or shoulder discomfort arises, swap to neutral-grip variations and adjust loads.

Sample 4-week micro-cycle example (Weeks 1–4)
- Week 1: 4 sessions; emphasis on learning and technique; RPE around 6–7
- Week 2: Add small load increase; maintain 4x sessions
- Week 3: Add one set to primary lifts where tolerating; keep RPE 6–7
- Week 4: Deload with lighter loads and technique focus; maintain movement quality

If you’d like, I can tailor this further to her exact equipment, preferred exercises, and any pregnancy symptom considerations, and provide a week-by-week printable sheet with daily workout cards.
